headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because slim can read/write broad filesystem and egress network, while dbt-core touches warehouse data and can call warehouse APIs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared clipboard, MCP, or direct ingestion channel is documented. However, slim reads filesystem artifacts and emits interactive CLI output, while dbt-core can call a data warehouse and handle warehouse data; a manual copy-paste bridge could carry malicious instructions. The pathway is limited and not default.
conditions: IF an operator copies slim output into dbt-core prompts or SQL files
IF dbt-core is configured to treat file contents as instructions
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate terminals and avoid copy-paste between them
Review any pasted text before execution
Use read-only exports for dbt inputs
Add a manual approval step before dbt runs generated content

B_data_leakage.rationale: slim touches filesystem artifacts, environment variables, certificate private keys, and registry credentials, while dbt-core touches data warehouse data and can call a warehouse API. In default use, a shared workspace or copied artifacts could expose sensitive material from slim into dbt workflows or logs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible even without a documented shared filesystem.
conditions: IF slim artifacts are placed in a workspace that dbt-core reads
IF dbt-core logs or uploads warehouse-derived outputs containing sensitive fields
mitigations: Store slim outputs in a separate directory from dbt projects
Redact secrets before any handoff
Disable verbose logging for both tools
Use least-privilege warehouse credentials for dbt
Delete temporary artifacts after each run

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core has allowlisted network egress and warehouse API access, while slim has broad network egress plus filesystem write and shell execution. They do not share a documented lock or shared-state model, so overlapping writes are not proven; still, both can mutate external resources in ways that can conflict if pointed at the same workspace or registry inputs.
conditions: IF both agents target the same filesystem path or artifact directory
IF dbt-core and slim are run against the same external resource without coordination
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize runs with a simple operator checklist
Avoid concurrent writes to shared artifacts
Use immutable inputs for dbt and slim where possible

D_cascading_error.rationale: slim can produce command-driven analysis artifacts, and dbt-core can act on warehouse data and API calls. If dbt consumes slim-generated outputs as authoritative without verification, errors can propagate into downstream transformations or warehouse actions. The pair is not documented as mutually validating, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF dbt-core ingests slim-generated files or stdout without validation
IF an operator uses slim output as the sole source for dbt model changes
mitigations: Require a human review of slim output before dbt use
Compare outputs against a known-good baseline
Use schema checks on any transferred artifacts
Separate analysis and execution steps

E_compliance.rationale: slim handles registry credentials, certificate private keys, and environment variables, while dbt-core handles data warehouse data. If regulated data or secrets are co-located in a shared workflow, retention or residency controls can diverge. No specific residency mismatch is documented, so this is a general compliance-gap risk rather than high severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the same workspace as slim artifacts
IF retention or deletion policies differ between warehouse data and container-analysis artifacts
mitigations: Separate regulated data from container-analysis outputs
Document retention periods for both tools
Purge temporary files after each session
Restrict access to credential-bearing artifacts
